newsitem.title: USA: ING Barings stays in NYC, will add 900 jobs.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings stays in NYC, will add 900 jobs.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki said Monday that ING Barings, an Anglo-Dutch financial concern, would remain in New York City.
The company will consolidate its offices in Manhattan for 900 employees and add 300 new jobs over the next two years and 600 more jobs over the next seven years, said Pataki.
ING, which considered moving all its "back office" operations out of the state, will now consolidate operations in midtown Manhattan on East 52 Street, said the governor.

The state said that, in consideration of the company's committment to create jobs, ING Barings now qualifies for $3.4 million in sales tax exemptions on capital improvements, $1.6 million in utility rate reductions and a $100,000 job training grant.
